technicalDispatch.title: Resolving MySQL Host 127.0.0.1 Access Denied in cPanel

sections.label: The problem
sections.body: Laravel on cPanel returned 'Host 127.0.0.1 is not allowed to connect' when the app tried to reach MySQL.

sections.label: Root cause
sections.body: MySQL user was bound to a specific host; cPanel's PHP/CLI often resolves as 127.0.0.1, which wasn't granted.

sections.label: Fix
sections.body: Created a MySQL user with host '%' (or 'localhost' / '127.0.0.1' as needed) and granted privileges. Updated .env DB_HOST to match.

sections.label: Lessons learned
sections.body: Always align DB_USER host with how the app connects; Remote MySQL in cPanel shows allowed hosts.

sections.label: Preventative strategy
sections.body: Document DB setup in the project README and use the same credentials in staging so this is caught before production.
